findings.title: A release-only main breaks the release workflow's dry run, the scheduled workflows, Dependabot and post-release installs
findings.claim: The owner checklist keeps `main` behind until a release is published ('main never names a version that has no release', step 5 'Fast-forward main to the tag'). On GitHub, `main` is the default branch, and several features read only the default branch: `workflow_dispatch` (checklist step 2), schedules (`advisories.yml`, `toolchain.yml`), the `dependabot.yml` config, and the branch that Dependabot and security-update PRs target. The design also never says where development merges after v0.1.0. And the `--branch main` source-build fallback is offered in exactly the state where `main` holds no code.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Owner checklist': 'main never names a version that has no release ... 2. Run Release by hand on that branch: a dry run. 3. Tag ... 5. Fast-forward main to the tag'. DR-58: 'A departure from Iris: the owner tags the release branch and fast-forwards main after publishing'. Packaging: 'When git ls-remote shows no such tag ... offers --branch main'. Verified here: `gh api repos/doodla/planroom` gives default_branch main, public; `git log origin/main` is only '3227142 Initial commit'; `.github/workflows/` on the work branch holds only ci.yml. Assumed from GitHub's documentation, not checked live: workflow_dispatch needs the workflow file on the default branch, schedules run from the default branch, and dependabot.yml is read from the default branch and its PRs target it. KICKOFF requires a release workflow, Dependabot, and 'the exact clicks I owe'. Iris's order is merge first, then tag [iris-release-bar §3]. plugin-packaging §5: the plugin version resolves from plugin.json.
findings.failure_scenario: (1) At v0.1.0, the owner follows step 2. Release isn't listed under Actions because release.yml isn't on main, so the dry run can't be run. (2) advisories.yml and toolchain.yml never run before the first release, and Dependabot stays off. Once main is fast-forwarded, Dependabot PRs merge into main, main diverges from the next release branch, and step 5's fast-forward fails. (3) After v0.1.0, any feature merged to main keeps version 0.1.0 but changes the committed mod bundle and the catalogue hash in engine.env. A fresh `/plugin marketplace add doodla/planroom` downloads the v0.1.0 engine, the mod's hash check fails, and the user sees 'Run /reload-plugins', which can't fix it. (4) Someone installs from a pre-release branch URL. The tag is missing, so the resolver offers `cargo install --git ... --branch main`, which fails because main has no Cargo.toml.
findings.proposed_fix: Write a branch-model decision record. Recommended: (a) keep `main` as the default and integration branch, so workflow_dispatch, schedules and Dependabot work, and follow Iris's order (merge, green CI on main, dry run, tag on main). (b) Between releases, main carries `X.Y.Z-dev`. The resolver treats a `-dev` version as having no release asset and goes straight to the source-build preflight and card. (c) Stable installs come from a `stable` branch the owner fast-forwards to each tag, if WS8 confirms a marketplace source can name a ref; otherwise document that an install from main is a dev build. (d) Replace the `--branch main` fallback with the plugin's own ref, `--rev`, read from the marketplace clone. Update the owner checklist and releasing.md, and add a test that the checklist's steps match the release.yml triggers.

findings.title: `setsid` doesn't exist on macOS, so prefetch --detach and build --detach fail on both macOS targets
findings.claim: The resolver detaches `prefetch --detach` and `build --detach` 'under `setsid`'. macOS ships no `setsid(1)`; it's a util-linux tool. The mod launches both through `$.process.run`, which blocks on any child that keeps stdio open. So on macOS the engine's first-use resolve, and the source-build fallback, either fail with 'command not found' or hang the call, or the child gets killed on reload.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: '`prefetch --detach` and `build --detach` run under `setsid`, log to DATA_ROOT/logs/engine.log and write a pid file, so a reload doesn't kill them'. DR-58 says the same. mod-api §7: '`process.run` blocks on a child that keeps stdio open'; 'A daemon launched with run must detach and close its stdio'; 'It is unverified whether the engine kills the child's process group or only its pid'. KICKOFF constraint: 'The release workflow builds the engine for Linux and macOS'; S14 step 2: 'The engine resolves on first use'. That macOS lacks setsid is platform knowledge; I didn't check it here, since this is a Linux container.
findings.failure_scenario: On a fresh macOS install, the mod's `session.start` finds no engine and runs `scripts/planroom prefetch --detach`. `setsid: command not found` makes the fetch fail. The pane goes to `failed`, and its retry runs the same command. The toolchain preflight passes, so the person accepts 'Build the engine from source?', and `build --detach` fails the same way. Planroom never starts on either Mac target. If the implementer instead drops the detach on macOS, `process.run` blocks until its timeout, or the download dies on the next /reload-plugins.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify a portable detach. Use `setsid` when present. Otherwise use `perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::setsid(); exec @ARGV'` (perl ships with macOS 15) or a double fork, `( cmd </dev/null >>log 2>&1 & )`, with stdio closed. Name this in the resolver's design and in DR-58. Add `tests/installer/run.sh::detach_returns_at_once_and_survives_parent_exit`, run on macos-15 in the `installer (os)` job, and spike it on macOS in WS5 next to A-14.

findings.title: Debounced backups in a process-per-command engine can lose a person's last edits
findings.claim: DR-53 promises 'Nothing a person authored lives only in store.db', but it appends to the backup 'after each person-authored commit, debounced to one write per 5 s'. Writers are short-lived CLI processes: the mod runs one `planroom` process per command (DR-6), and there's no daemon (DR-1). A debounce inside a process that exits within milliseconds either drops the pending append or postpones it to some later commit. The design also doesn't say where the backup cursor lives, or how concurrent writer processes avoid gaps and duplicates.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Store schema': 'Nothing a person authored lives only in store.db [DR-53]. After each person-authored commit, debounced to one write per 5 s, the engine appends the new events to DATA_ROOT/backups/<workspace_id>/events.ndjson'. DR-6: 'the mod runs commands with $.process.run (argv and env in, one JSON envelope out)'. DR-1: 'no engine daemon'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did'. DR-53 cites `git clean -xfd` as the motivating loss.
findings.failure_scenario: A person regroups two components and renames a third from the pane within 4 s, which is three `planroom edit` processes. The first appends, and the next two fall inside the debounce window. Their processes exit, and nothing else commits that day. Later `git clean -xfd` deletes `.planroom/`. `scan` offers 'Restore 1 edit', and the rename and the second regroup are gone. If two processes append the same cursor range concurrently, the backup instead holds duplicates, which a naive restore replays twice.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the debounce for person-authored commits: an ndjson append of a few events is cheap. Keep a `backup_seq` cursor in the store's meta table. After each commit, the writer appends events with `seq > backup_seq` under an `flock` on the backup file, fsyncs, then advances the cursor. Any later process catches up the gap. Restore dedupes by event id. Add `backup.rs::the_last_edit_before_exit_is_backed_up` and `concurrent_writers_leave_no_gap_or_duplicate`.

findings.title: S14's live release-asset run can't be reached through the documented resolver, and its needed override is unconstrained
findings.claim: S14's evidence path needs a fresh session installed from the local repo to resolve the engine 'through the release-asset path against a locally built, checksummed asset'. In the documented order, the dev checkout (step 2) outranks the download (step 4). The download URL is the fixed GitHub tag, which doesn't exist before the owner publishes, and the only documented override is `$PLANROOM_ENGINE`, which skips the download entirely. The CI suite's '127.0.0.1 server' implies a base-URL override that no contract documents. The checksum comes from that same base URL, so such an override amounts to full code-execution trust, unless it is limited to https, and http only for loopback, as Iris's install.sh does.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging, resolver order: '1. $PLANROOM_ENGINE; 2. the dev checkout, when <script dir>/../../Cargo.toml exists ...; 4. a sha256-verified download ... for the fixed tag vVERSION'; 'It needs nothing from its environment but optional overrides'. None of the overrides is listed in contracts.md Configuration. feature_list.json S14 evidence: 'through the source-build path live, built from the checkout ..., and through the release-asset path against a locally built, checksummed asset'. S14 CI path: 'the resolver against a 127.0.0.1 server'. iris-release-bar §3: install.sh allows 'http only for an http:// test base URL'. KICKOFF S14.2 and principle 2 ('stable, typed, documented interfaces').
findings.failure_scenario: The evidence run first does the live source build, which leaves `target/release/planroom` with a matching hash. The second run, meant to exercise the asset path, resolves through step 2 again and never downloads. With `target/` deleted, step 4 fetches github.com/doodla/planroom/releases/download/v0.1.0/..., which returns 404. The tier A evidence step can't be recorded. An ad hoc `PLANROOM_*_URL` added to make the test pass, with no scheme or host rule, lets any process environment point the resolver at an attacker's archive and its matching SHA256SUMS.
findings.proposed_fix: Document the resolver's environment as a contract: `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` (https only, with http allowed only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost) and `PLANROOM_RESOLVE=release|checkout|auto`, which picks the steps. `status --json` reports which step resolved and from where. Put these in contracts.md Configuration and the guides' install page, and use them in S14's evidence steps. Add installer tests: `base_url_refuses_plain_http_to_a_non_loopback_host` and `resolve_release_skips_the_checkout`.

findings.title: A dev build whose hash doesn't match falls through to a cached release engine, and the advice shown is wrong
findings.claim: When neither `target/release` nor `target/debug` reports engine.env's catalogue hash, the resolver falls through to the cache (step 3). The cache check is only the `.ok` sha256, with no catalogue check, so it returns a released engine with a different catalogue. The mod then shows 'Run /reload-plugins', which can't help: the fix is `cargo xtask gen` plus a rebuild. Separately, `serve --detach` drains a same-version `serve` with another hash, so a dev session and a release session in one workspace keep draining each other's server.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging, step 2 'whose version --json reports the catalogue hash in engine.env'; step 3 'the cache ... with a .ok stamp holding its sha256'; Mod wiring step 2: 'A mismatch shows one status line, "This Planroom engine doesn't match the plugin. Run /reload-plugins"'; Version handshake: drains 'one of the same version with another catalogue hash (a dev build)'. KICKOFF `<process>` 4: the walking skeleton loads 'through the plugin install from day one, with the engine built from source'.
findings.failure_scenario: After v0.1.0, an agent in this repo edits a command and runs `cargo xtask gen`, but not a release build. Its next session resolves the cached v0.1.0 engine. The pane says to reload plugins, the reload changes nothing, and the agent burns turns. Meanwhile a canvas tab on the other session's `serve` loses its token every time either session runs `serve --detach`.
findings.proposed_fix: In a checkout, a hash mismatch never falls through to the cache or a download. It returns `version_mismatch` with the build command, for example 'Run cargo build -p planroom' or the build card. The mod's mismatch line names the fix for the cause it detects: plugin stale means /reload-plugins, engine stale means rebuild. `serve --detach` drains a same-version server only when its own binary is newer by mtime, or leaves it alone and reports the conflict once.

findings.title: The `cargo install --git` fallback builds an engine without the canvas, and its fix page points at a checkout the user doesn't have
findings.claim: For a plugin installed from a marketplace cache, the source-build fallback is `cargo install --git REPO --tag vVERSION planroom`. That build never runs `cargo xtask gen --canvas`, and `target/canvas/` isn't committed, so the binary has no canvas. Its fix page says 'Run cargo xtask gen --canvas, then rebuild', but there is no checkout to run it in. The canvas (S13) and `share` (S11) are unavailable, with no actionable next step.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Local server and live stream': 'A binary built without it, such as cargo install --git on a machine without Node, serves one engine-rendered page ... "Run cargo xtask gen --canvas, then rebuild"'; 'share ... without it fails with not_found'. repo-layout.md generated directories: `target/canvas/` is 'Committed? no'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never show a blank state'; KICKOFF constraint: 'The fallback is cargo install --git or a local build'.
findings.failure_scenario: A user behind a proxy that blocks release-asset downloads but allows git takes the build card. The engine works, but `/room open` shows the fix page, and `/room share` fails, both naming a command the user can't run.
findings.proposed_fix: For a cached install, the resolver's build clones the tag into DATA_ROOT/src/vVERSION, runs `cargo xtask gen --canvas` there when Node and pnpm pass the preflight, then `cargo build --release --locked`. Without Node, the preflight says in one line that the canvas needs Node 22 and pnpm, and offers the build anyway. The fix page's text comes from the engine and names `scripts/planroom build` rather than xtask when no checkout exists.

findings.title: Pruning the engine cache on every resolve breaks sessions still running the previous version
findings.claim: 'A successful resolve prunes older versions from the cache', while each mod resolves once and keeps the binary path in `$.state`. After `/plugin update`, sessions that haven't restarted still run the old plugin and call the deleted path, so every focus refresh and tool call fails until restart, even when the store schema didn't change.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: 'A successful resolve prunes older versions from the cache'; Mod wiring step 2: 'Resolve the engine once ... stores the binary path ... in $.state'; plugin-packaging §3: data dirs persist across updates, and plugins load per session.
findings.failure_scenario: Two sessions run v0.1.0. The user updates the plugin and opens a third session, which resolves v0.1.1 and deletes engine/0.1.0/. The first two sessions' next `process.run` fails with ENOENT, and their panes show `failed`. Retry re-downloads 0.1.0, which the next v0.1.1 resolve deletes again.
findings.proposed_fix: Prune only versions whose `last_used` stamp, touched on each resolve, is older than 7 days, and never a version named by a live `serve.json` or pid file. The mod re-resolves once on ENOENT before showing `failed`. Add installer test `prune_keeps_a_recently_used_version`.

findings.title: There is no upgrade path for users, and 'Restart this session' doesn't upgrade anything
findings.claim: Auto-update is off for third-party marketplaces, and the design has no 'Upgrade Planroom' guide or command (only 'Remove Planroom'). An older engine that meets a newer store tells the person to 'Restart this session to use Planroom vX'. That works only if the plugin is already updated. When the newer writer was a dev build, the `--branch main` fallback or `$PLANROOM_ENGINE`, a restart reloads the same old plugin, and the person gets the same message again.
findings.evidence: plugin-packaging §5: 'Auto-update is off for third-party marketplaces [guide]'; the version resolves from plugin.json. architecture.md 'Version handshake' and DR-53: 'An older engine meeting a newer store exits with schema_mismatch, and the mod shows "Restart this session to use Planroom vX" once'. architecture.md Packaging lists only the 'Remove Planroom' guide. KICKOFF `<stance>`: 'packaging, ... migrations, upgrades ... are yours to handle'.
findings.failure_scenario: A user who once accepted the `--branch main` build now has a store migrated to schema v3. After switching back to the released plugin, every session says 'Restart this session to use Planroom v0.2.0', and restarting changes nothing. The way out, `doctor --restore`, is never named.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `docs/guides/upgrade.md`: `/plugin marketplace update planroom`, `/plugin update planroom@planroom`, restart. Make `schema_mismatch` carry the writer's version and the installed plugin version. The mod names the update commands when the plugin is older, and `planroom doctor --restore BACKUP` when no released plugin is that new. Test that the message names the right action in each case.

findings.title: No defined behaviour when a skill or agent calls the resolver during a prefetch, or when mods are off and the download fails
findings.claim: The fetch lock says when a lock counts as stale (a dead pid, or 15 minutes) but not how long a resolver run waits on a live one. Skills and agents run the resolver through the Bash tool, which times out at 2 minutes by default. With mods off there is no card, so step 5, 'the source build, after a person's card', has no defined output for the Bash path.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: 'The fetch lock ... breaks it when kill -0 fails for that pid or the lock is older than 15 minutes'; step 5 'the source build, after a person's card'; Mod 'With mods off ... the resolver fetches the engine on its first call'. plugin-packaging Top risks 2: 'fail fast with clear stderr'.
findings.failure_scenario: In the first session, the mod's prefetch is downloading through a slow proxy, and the model runs the `room` skill. The resolver blocks on the lock until the Bash tool kills it at 120 s, and the model sees an empty timeout instead of an envelope. With mods off and no release yet, the resolver's output for a missing asset is unspecified, so an agent can't tell 'build needed' from 'broken'.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify it: a non-mod caller waits at most 20 s on a live lock, then exits non-zero with one JSON envelope on stdout (`engine_fetching`, with progress and a retry_after_ms). When the download fails, a non-mod caller gets `engine_unavailable`, naming `scripts/planroom build` and its estimated time, and never starts a build itself. Add both to the error registry and to tests/installer.

findings.title: engine.env's authorship contradicts itself, and nothing generates the version bump
findings.claim: DR-28 says 'release writes plugin/scripts/engine.env', and repo-layout says its version is 'written at release'. Yet release.yml's `verify` checks engine.env against the tag, and `publish` can only create a release, not commit. So engine.env must be committed by the bump. The version appears in Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, plugin.json, every package.json and engine.env, plus the CHANGELOG move, and no `cargo xtask` command writes them. That is hand-editing across many files, by an agent restricted to xtask commands.
findings.evidence: decisions.md DR-28 Consequences: 'release writes plugin/scripts/engine.env'; repo-layout.md Plugin layout: 'PLANROOM_ENGINE_VERSION, PLANROOM_REPO (written at release)'; architecture.md Release workflow 1: 'verify ... checks that the tag is v plus the version in Cargo.toml, plugin.json, every package.json and engine.env'; repo-layout 'Agents and CI use only these commands'; KICKOFF 'Prepare them, and list exactly what I need to click'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reads DR-28 and makes release.yml write engine.env at build time. The tagged commit's engine.env then still names the old version. Every git install of the release fetches the previous engine, and the catalogue-hash check fails for all users. Or a hand bump misses one package.json, and `verify` fails only after the owner has pushed the tag, which per Iris must never be moved.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct DR-28 and repo-layout: engine.env is generated by `cargo xtask gen` and committed in the bump commit. Add `cargo xtask gen --version X.Y.Z`, which writes every manifest, refreshes Cargo.lock, moves `[Unreleased]` to the dated section, and regenerates engine.env. Run `check-tag-version.sh` against the workspace version in `cargo xtask check`, so a partial bump fails before anyone tags.

findings.title: No MSRV job, and the CI target matrix is drifting from the Iris bar
findings.claim: The source-build preflight accepts any `cargo` 'at or above the workspace's rust-version'. But no CI job builds at that version, and `cargo install --git` uses the user's default toolchain, not the repo's rust-toolchain.toml. Iris has an `msrv` job and tests on macos-15-intel. Planroom has neither. The committed ci.yml skeleton also builds x86_64-apple-darwin on macos-15 (arm), while the docs say macos-15-intel.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: 'cargo at or above the workspace's rust-version'; iris-release-bar §2: 'msrv | ubuntu-24.04 | Reads rust-version ... cargo check ... cargo test' and 'test (os) ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, macos-15-intel'; repo-layout CI table: 'macos-15-intel for x86_64-apple-darwin'; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` release-dry-run matrix: '{ target: x86_64-apple-darwin, os: macos-15 }'. KICKOFF: 'Release bar. Match doodla/iris'.
findings.failure_scenario: rust-version says 1.89, but the code uses an API stabilised in 1.95. A user on 1.90 passes the preflight, accepts the 4-minute build card, and gets a compile error. Once the dry-run job is enabled as committed, the Intel macOS archive is cross-compiled on arm, so it's never executed or smoke-tested before release.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `cargo xtask check --msrv`, a job that builds and tests at `rust-version`, or set rust-version to the pinned 1.97 and say so. Have the resolver's build pass `+<rust-version>` when rustup is present. Align ci.yml with repo-layout (macos-15-intel) and add macos-15-intel to `test (os)`, or record why not.

findings.title: Iris art spend has no record or cap, so the final report can't show it
findings.claim: KICKOFF caps Iris at under $5 and requires the final report to give Iris spend. The design's one build-wide spend record covers only Jev, gateway and `sample` calls. The Iris art line has no ledger, no `--max-cost` rule and no test.
findings.evidence: KICKOFF constraints: 'Iris ... makes all images ... Spend under $5, with the prompts committed next to the images'; definition of done: 'Iris and Jev spend'; verified facts: '--dry-run --json shows the cost first, and --max-cost caps it'. architecture.md 'Spend guards': the record covers 'Jev, gateway and sample spend'; Milestones M5: 'Iris art finish ..., under $5 with prompts | R15 | 2'.
findings.failure_scenario: Several regenerations of the hero and empty-state art add up past $5 unnoticed, or the final report states an Iris figure with no evidence behind it.
findings.proposed_fix: Have each Iris run go through a recorded step: a dry-run cost, then `-m MODEL --max-cost` with whatever headroom is left, appending `{at, image, model, cost_usd, prompt_path}` to `docs/art/spend.jsonl`. Add a `docs.rs` test that every image under docs/art has a prompt and a spend row, and that the total is under $5.

verdicts.reason: The owner checklist keeps main behind the release branch and only fast-forwards it after publishing. Nothing in the reviewed docs names a different default or integration branch. On GitHub, workflow_dispatch needs the workflow file on the default branch, schedules run from the default branch, and dependabot.yml is read from it. So at v0.1.0, checklist step 2 (the hand-run dry run) can't be clicked, and advisories.yml, toolchain.yml and Dependabot stay inert until the first release. Dependabot PRs then target main, which breaks step 5's fast-forward. The design also says nowhere where development merges after v0.1.0. The --branch main fallback is offered in exactly the state where main holds only the initial commit. The tag push itself still triggers release.yml from the tagged commit, so publishing isn't blocked. But the owner's click list is wrong, and the Dependabot and scheduled-audit requirements from KICKOFF go unmet, so it stays material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md 'Owner checklist': '`main` never names a version that has no release ... 2. Run Release by hand on that branch: a dry run ... 5. Fast-forward `main` to the tag'. DR-58 says the same: 'the owner tags the release branch and fast-forwards `main` after publishing'. repo-layout.md:292: 'Scheduled: advisories.yml ... toolchain.yml ... release.yml runs ... as a dry run on workflow_dispatch'. architecture.md Packaging: 'offers `--branch main`'. `git branch -a` shows main and origin/main; .github/workflows holds only ci.yml. repo-layout's decision-record gate uses 'BASE is the fork point from main', which also assumes main is the integration branch. KICKOFF: 'Dependabot', 'a release workflow', 'list exactly what I need to click'. The GitHub default-branch behaviour comes from GitHub's documentation; I didn't check it live.

verdicts.reason: The design depends on `setsid` for both detached paths and names no portable alternative. macOS has no setsid(1); it's a util-linux tool. Both macOS targets are required, and the mod's first-use path runs `prefetch --detach`, so that path fails on macOS. The installer job on macos-15 would probably catch it during implementation, but as written the design is wrong for two of the four required targets.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: '`prefetch --detach` and `build --detach` run under `setsid`, log to `DATA_ROOT/logs/engine.log` and write a pid file'. DR-58 Decision: 'Prefetch and build run detached under `setsid`'. architecture.md Mod wiring 2: 'If the engine is missing, it runs `scripts/planroom prefetch --detach`'. KICKOFF:237: 'builds the engine for Linux and macOS, on x86_64 and arm64'. That macOS lacks setsid is platform knowledge; I couldn't test it in this Linux container.

verdicts.reason: The backup is debounced to 'one write per 5 s', but the writers are short-lived CLI processes and there's no daemon. Nothing defines a backup cursor or a catch-up step, and nothing defines which process flushes a debounced append. So the last edits before a quiet period can be missing from the backup, and those are exactly the edits the backup exists to protect after `git clean -xfd` (principle 1, data loss). contracts.md even contradicts the debounce: it says the backup is 'appended after each person-authored commit'. doctor's staleness warning only detects the gap after the fact.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:486 and DR-53: 'After each person-authored commit, debounced to one write per 5 s, the engine appends the new events to `DATA_ROOT/backups/<workspace_id>/events.ndjson`'. contracts.md:311: 'appended after each person-authored commit' (no debounce). architecture.md:154: `planroom <cmd>` is 'one command' per process. architecture.md:486: '`planroom doctor` warns when the newest backup is older than the last person-authored event' (detection only, no repair). The docs specify no backup_seq cursor or flock.

verdicts.reason: S14 is tier A. Its evidence path needs a release-asset resolve against a locally built asset, and its CI path needs 'the resolver against a 127.0.0.1 server'. The final resolver design documents no base-URL override. Step 4 is 'for the fixed tag vVERSION', and step 2 (the dev checkout) outranks it in a local-repo install. The research candidates had `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` with an https-only rule (http only for 127.0.0.1), but it didn't survive into architecture.md or contracts.md. contracts.md Configuration lists no resolver variable at all.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md Packaging: 'It needs nothing from its environment but optional overrides ... 1. `$PLANROOM_ENGINE`; 2. the dev checkout ...; 4. a sha256-verified download ... for the fixed tag `vVERSION`'. feature_list.json S14 ci_path: 'the resolver against a 127.0.0.1 server holding a locally built, checksummed archive'; evidence_path: 'through the release-asset path against a locally built, checksummed asset'. contracts.md 'Configuration' has no resolver keys. research/arch/candidate-extensibility.md:1936 had `${PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL:-...}` with '`curl --proto =https` (http only for a `127.0.0.1` test base)', which was dropped from the final design.

verdicts.reason: The finding is real and correctly rated minor. Step 2 skips a dev build whose hash doesn't match, and step 3 checks only the `.ok` sha256, not the catalogue, so a cached release engine is returned. The mod's only mismatch text is 'Run /reload-plugins', and the version_mismatch fallback's band action names only /reload-plugins. The version handshake drains any same-version `serve` with another catalogue hash, so two sessions with different catalogues keep draining each other's server.
